title: wsgnstat: the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution
text: line, skew generalised normal distribution two-piece exponential-power density f(x)=cexp⁡{−(λ±|x−μ|σ)β},c=1σ(1/λ1+1/λ2)Γ(1+1/β), f(x) = c \, \exp\!\left\{-\left(\frac{\lambda_{\pm} |x - \mu|}{\sigma}\right)^{\beta}\right\}, \qquad c = \frac{1}{\sigma \, (1/\lambda_1 + 1/\lambda_2) \, \Gamma(1 + 1/\beta)}, λ1\lambda_1 right location μ\mu λ2\lambda_2 left. scale mixture uniform variable generalised gamma variable, rsgn() draws . shape β>0\beta > 0 governs tails (β=2\beta = 2 Gaussian, β=1\beta = 1 Laplace-like, smaller values heavier), pair (λ1,λ2)(\lambda_1, \lambda_2) asymmetry: mass left μ\mu λ1/(λ1+λ2)\lambda_1 / (\lambda_1 + \lambda_2). Wrapping onto circle sums line density turns, fW(θ)=∑kf(θ+2πk)f_W(\theta) = \sum_k f(\theta + 2\pi k). circle package uses identified parameterisation λ1=λ\lambda_1 = \lambda, λ2=1−λ\lambda_2 = 1 - \lambda σ=λ(1−λ)\sigma = \sqrt{\lambda (1 - \lambda)}, circular law three parameters: location mu, tail parameter beta skewness lam, lam = 0.5 symmetric. skew law mu junction two pieces, mean direction. Wrapped densities three tail parameters, symmetric (solid) skew (dashed).
code: th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 721) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) for (b in c(0.8, 1.5, 3)) {   plot(th, dwsgn(th, mu = pi, beta = b, lam = 0.5), type = "l", ylim = c(0, 1.2),        xlab = "angle (radians)", ylab = "density", main = paste("beta =", b))   lines(th, dwsgn(th, mu = pi, beta = b, lam = 0.25), lty = 2) } par(op)

title: wsgnstat: the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution
text: four functions follow R’s usual naming. distribution function measured anticlockwise angle zero computed exactly, sum turns incomplete gamma functions, needs numerical quadrature; quantile function inverts . distribution function agrees direct numerical integration density, density integrates one circle: Draws identified parameterisation come rwsgn(); rsgn() draws line, wraps asked, (σ,λ1,λ2)(\sigma, \lambda_1, \lambda_2). sample 5000 draws wrapped density overlaid. Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance sample exact distribution function confirms agreement:
code: mu <- 1 beta <- 1.5 lam <- 0.3 dwsgn(c(0.5, 1, 2), mu, beta, lam) #> [1] 0.2607334 0.5077476 0.2989011 pwsgn(c(0.5, 1, 2), mu, beta, lam) #> [1] 0.07806267 0.27633042 0.69219129 qwsgn(c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), mu, beta, lam) #> [1] 0.5779239 1.4711739 3.1037257 c(pwsgn = pwsgn(2, mu, beta, lam),   integrate = integrate(dwsgn, 0, 2, mu = mu, beta = beta, lam = lam)$value,   total = integrate(dwsgn, 0, 2 * pi, mu = mu, beta = beta, lam = lam)$value) #>     pwsgn integrate     total  #> 0.6921913 0.6921913 0.9999999 set.seed(1) x <- rwsgn(5000, mu, beta, lam) hist(x, breaks = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 49), freq = FALSE, main = "",      xlab = "angle (radians)") curve(dwsgn(x, mu, beta, lam), 0, 2 * pi, add = TRUE, lwd = 2) u <- sort(pwsgn(x, mu, beta, lam)) n <- length(u) c(KS = max(pmax((1:n) / n - u, u - (0:(n - 1)) / n)), five_per_cent_critical = 1.358 / sqrt(n)) #>                     KS five_per_cent_critical  #>             0.01316301             0.01920502

title: wsgnstat: the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution
text: β=2\beta = 2 line law two-piece (split) normal, circular law wrapped split normal; lam = 0.5 well, σ=1/2\sigma = 1/2 rate one sides, line law N(0,1/2)N(0, 1/2) circular law wrapped normal σ=1/2\sigma = 1/\sqrt{2}. reductions can checked densities built directly dnorm(): trigonometric moments wrapped normal exp⁡(−p2σ2/2)=exp⁡(−p2/4)\exp(-p^2 \sigma^2 / 2) = \exp(-p^2/4), engine reproduces characteristic function: identified parameterisation concentration symmetric members tied tail parameter, wrapped normal reached β=2\beta = 2 one σ=1/2\sigma = 1/\sqrt{2}; skew members β=2\beta = 2 wrapped split normals matching scale. wrapped skew-normal Pewsey (2000) skews normal differently, factor 2Φ(αz)2\Phi(\alpha z) Azzalini’s construction rather two pieces. two families share wrapped normal, α=0\alpha = 0 β=2\beta = 2, lam = 0.5 : Away wrapped normal two skewing mechanisms give different shapes (two half-normals joined mode, normal density reweighted normal distribution function), neither family contains ’s skew members.
code: tt <- c(0.5, 2, 4.5) k <- -60:60 wrapped_normal <- vapply(tt, function(t) sum(dnorm(t + 2 * pi * k, 0, sqrt(1 / 2))), 0) rbind(wsgnstat = dwsgn(tt, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5), wrapped_normal = wrapped_normal) #>                     [,1]      [,2]       [,3] #> wsgnstat       0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806 #> wrapped_normal 0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806  ## wrapped split normal: standard deviation sigma / (sqrt(2) lam) on the right of mu and ## sigma / (sqrt(2) (1 - lam)) on the left, with left mass lam l <- 0.3 s <- sqrt(l * (1 - l)) split_normal <- function(x) {   sr <- s / (sqrt(2) * l)   sl <- s / (sqrt(2) * (1 - l))   ifelse(x >= 0, 2 * (1 - l) * dnorm(x, 0, sr), 2 * l * dnorm(x, 0, sl)) } wrapped_split <- vapply(tt, function(t) sum(split_normal(t + 2 * pi * k)), 0) rbind(wsgnstat = dwsgn(tt, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = l), wrapped_split_normal = wrapped_split) #>                           [,1]       [,2]         [,3] #> wsgnstat             0.4645507 0.09312363 0.0003979992 #> wrapped_split_normal 0.4645507 0.09312363 0.0003979992 tm <- trig_moments(4, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5) rbind(engine = tm$A, closed_form = exp(-(1:4)^2 / 4)) #>                  [,1]      [,2]      [,3]       [,4] #> engine      0.7788008 0.3678794 0.1053992 0.01831564 #> closed_form 0.7788008 0.3678794 0.1053992 0.01831564 dwsn <- function(theta, xi, omega, alpha, k = -60:60) {   vapply(theta, function(t) {     z <- (t + 2 * pi * k - xi) / omega     sum(2 / omega * dnorm(z) * pnorm(alpha * z))   }, 0) } rbind(wrapped_skew_normal_alpha0 = dwsn(tt, 0, sqrt(1 / 2), 0),       wsgnstat = dwsgn(tt, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5)) #>                                 [,1]      [,2]       [,3] #> wrapped_skew_normal_alpha0 0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806 #> wsgnstat                   0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806

title: wsgnstat: the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution
text: Two estimators provided. fit_wsgn_trig() matches first two sample trigonometric moments population values (minimum distance, sandwich standard errors); population moments come characteristic function, evaluated absolutely convergent integrals therefore available every β>0\beta > 0, including β≤1\beta \le 1, Fox-Wright series representation converge everywhere. fit_wsgn_mle() maximises wrapped likelihood, starting moment estimate; standard errors, asked , come parametric bootstrap, observed information unstable near cusp density develops β\beta approaches one. moment estimates lie within 2.5 standard errors truth every coordinate, likelihood estimates within 0.048 every coordinate, heavy-tailed shape (β=0.8\beta = 0.8) characteristic function reached integral route. Bootstrap standard errors likelihood fit refit model per replicate; small run lighter-tailed member:
code: truth <- c(mu = 4, beta = 0.8, lam = 0.6) set.seed(17) y <- rwsgn(2000, truth["mu"], truth["beta"], truth["lam"]) ft <- fit_wsgn_trig(y) fm <- fit_wsgn_mle(y) round(rbind(truth = truth, moments = ft$par, moments_se = ft$se, likelihood = fm$par), 3) #>               mu  beta   lam #> truth      4.000 0.800 0.600 #> moments    4.202 0.809 0.723 #> moments_se 0.092 0.030 0.050 #> likelihood 4.048 0.780 0.646 truth2 <- c(mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) set.seed(18) y2 <- rwsgn(500, truth2["mu"], truth2["beta"], truth2["lam"]) fb <- fit_wsgn_mle(y2, B = 30) round(rbind(truth = truth2, estimate = fb$par, bootstrap_se = fb$se), 3) #>                 mu  beta   lam #> truth        1.000 1.500 0.300 #> estimate     0.957 1.459 0.289 #> bootstrap_se 0.063 0.075 0.028

what: An application: wind directions at Col de la Roa
title: wsgnstat: the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution
text: wind data ‘circular’ package hold 310 wind directions, radians, recorded meteorological station Italian Alps January March 2001 (Agostinelli 2007). section runs ‘circular’ installed. comparison, wrapped normal wrapped Cauchy laws fitted maximum likelihood ‘circular’ package, three fits set side side log-likelihood AIC. Wind directions fitted wrapped skew generalised normal density. goodness--fit look uses probability integral transform: correct model, pwsgn() fitted parameters carries data uniform values (0,1)(0, 1). Kuiper’s statistic suits circle depend origin placed. reference distribution ignores estimation parameters, p-value approximate (conservative). Probability-probability plot fitted model. modified Kuiper statistic, 3.5, lies well beyond 1 per cent critical value 2.001 (Stephens 1970), fitted law adequate description data absolute sense, although AIC 80 wrapped normal. three laws compared, smallest AIC belongs wrapped Cauchy law. comparison relative: fit judged best among three may still rejected, .
code: w <- as.numeric(wind_env$wind) %% (2 * pi) fw_t <- fit_wsgn_trig(w) fw <- fit_wsgn_mle(w) round(rbind(moments = fw_t$par, moments_se = fw_t$se, likelihood = fw$par), 3) #>                mu  beta   lam #> moments    -0.108 2.026 0.340 #> moments_se  0.167 0.458 0.076 #> likelihood  0.026 1.355 0.322 wc <- circular::circular(w, type = "angles", units = "radians", template = "none",                          modulo = "asis", zero = 0, rotation = "counter") f_wn <- circular::mle.wrappednormal(wc) f_wc <- circular::mle.wrappedcauchy(wc) ll <- c(wsgn = fw$logLik,         wrapped_normal = sum(log(circular::dwrappednormal(wc, f_wn$mu, f_wn$rho))),         wrapped_cauchy = sum(log(circular::dwrappedcauchy(wc, f_wc$mu, f_wc$rho)))) npar <- c(3, 2, 2) round(cbind(logLik = ll, parameters = npar, AIC = -2 * ll + 2 * npar), 1) #>                logLik parameters   AIC #> wsgn           -394.7          3 795.4 #> wrapped_normal -435.7          2 875.5 #> wrapped_cauchy -381.8          2 767.6 hist(w, breaks = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 37), freq = FALSE, main = "",      xlab = "direction (radians)") curve(dwsgn(x, fw$par["mu"], fw$par["beta"], fw$par["lam"]), 0, 2 * pi, add = TRUE, lwd = 2) u <- sort(pwsgn(w, fw$par["mu"], fw$par["beta"], fw$par["lam"])) n <- length(u) plot((1:n) / (n + 1), u, xlab = "uniform plotting position", ylab = "fitted distribution function",      pch = 20, cex = 0.6, asp = 1) abline(0, 1, lty = 2) V <- max((1:n) / n - u) + max(u - (0:(n - 1)) / n) Vstar <- V * (sqrt(n) + 0.155 + 0.24 / sqrt(n)) kuiper_p <- function(v) {   j <- 1:100   min(1, sum(2 * (4 * j^2 * v^2 - 1) * exp(-2 * j^2 * v^2))) } c(V = V, V_star = Vstar, approximate_p = kuiper_p(Vstar)) #>             V        V_star approximate_p  #>  1.970643e-01  3.502907e+00  2.114024e-09

code: ## reached through absolutely convergent integrals, so every beta > 0 is available, ## including beta <= 1, where the Fox-Wright series does not converge for all t cfsgn(0, 0, 1, 2, 0.5, 0.5) #> [1] 1+0i ## the normal member: exp(-t^2 / 4) for N(0, 1/2) t <- c(0.5, 1.5, 3) rbind(engine = Re(cfsgn(t, 0, 0.5, 2, 0.5, 0.5)), closed_form = exp(-t^2 / 4)) #>                  [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> engine      0.9394131 0.5697828 0.1053992 #> closed_form 0.9394131 0.5697828 0.1053992 ## a skew member with beta = 0.8, against the Fourier transform of the density x <- seq(-60, 60, length.out = 120001) f <- dsgn(x, 0, 1, 0.8, 0.8, 0.3) c(engine = cfsgn(1.1, 0, 1, 0.8, 0.8, 0.3),   quadrature = sum(exp(1i * 1.1 * x) * f) * (x[2] - x[1])) #>                engine            quadrature  #> 0.1129021-0.04099506i 0.1129029-0.04100219i

code: ## a skew member drawn on the circle as a radial curve about the unit circle th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 721) d <- dwsgn(th, mu = pi / 2, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) plot(cos(th), sin(th), type = "l", asp = 1, xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2),      xlab = "", ylab = "", lty = 3) lines((1 + d) * cos(th), (1 + d) * sin(th))  ## the density integrates to one over the circle sum(d[-1]) * (th[2] - th[1]) #> [1] 1 ## at beta = 2 with lam = 0.5 the circular law IS the wrapped normal ## with sigma = 1/sqrt(2), which anchors the wrapping machinery exactly tt <- c(0.5, 2.0, 4.5) wn <- vapply(tt, function(t) sum(dnorm(t + 2 * pi * (-80:80), 0, 1 / sqrt(2))), 0) rbind(wsgnstat = dwsgn(tt, 0, 2, 0.5), wrapped_normal = wn) #>                     [,1]      [,2]       [,3] #> wsgnstat       0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806 #> wrapped_normal 0.4393913 0.0103335 0.02346806

title: Distribution and quantile functions of the wrapped skew generalised normal distribution — pwsgn
code: ## the distribution function is the integral of the density pwsgn(2, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) #> [1] 0.6921913 integrate(dwsgn, 0, 2, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)$value #> [1] 0.6921913 ## the quantile function inverts it p <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95) q <- qwsgn(p, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) rbind(p, pwsgn(q, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)) #>   [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] #> p 0.05 0.25  0.5 0.75 0.95 #>   0.05 0.25  0.5 0.75 0.95 ## the curve rises from 0 to 1 around the circle th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 361) plot(th, pwsgn(th, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3), type = "l",      xlab = "angle (radians)", ylab = "distribution function")

title: Population trigonometric moments of the wrapped family (C back-end) — trig_moments
code: ## the reduction to the wrapped normal in the trigonometric moments: exp(-p^2 / 4) tm <- trig_moments(4, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5) rbind(engine = tm$A, closed_form = exp(-(1:4)^2 / 4)) #>                  [,1]      [,2]      [,3]       [,4] #> engine      0.7788008 0.3678794 0.1053992 0.01831564 #> closed_form 0.7788008 0.3678794 0.1053992 0.01831564 ## a skew member: the first moment against a large simulated sample tm1 <- trig_moments(1, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) set.seed(1) th <- rwsgn(1e5, mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3) rbind(population = c(tm1$A, tm1$B), sample = c(mean(cos(th)), mean(sin(th)))) #>                  [,1]      [,2] #> population 0.07582601 0.6411281 #> sample     0.07566699 0.6420514
